pairs.reason: B's type system is tighter: right-aligned type codes, stacked minute numerals, explicit 'Double-booked' label. C wraps '8:00 / AM' in the time column and truncates repeated type footers.
B names the 10:15 double booking in a red frame and lays out check-in as a checklist; A marks it with a small badge and gives the panel less structure.
C makes 'Finish Check In' the primary action, flags the double booking in the grid and in Needs attention, and uses a hyperlegible face with slashed zeros. A's double booking is quieter.

notes: All three restructure the screen the same basic way: a waiting-room list, the clinician grid, then an alerts-first detail panel. Differences are in finish. C appears to use a hyperlegible face with slashed zeros, a good fit for reading MRNs and times, but the time labels wrap and long blocks show truncated footers. B has the most finished component vocabulary, though some cells cut off reasons with an ellipsis. A is clean but more generic.
